analysis.summary: The cleanup PR should not be approved for 2026-10-15. CI only passes because the PR deletes test_replay_v1_reversal. When that test is kept, it fails on HEAD with "AssertionError: 0 != 5000". HEAD drops v1 without raising an error: run_job keeps only rows whose schema_version is in accepted_versions=["2"], so v1 rows are skipped with no exception (before_error and after_error are both null). The synthetic replays (no production data) show what that costs. NORTHSTAR historical_replay for 2026-09 falls from 125000 to 40000 cents, losing 85000 (A-1, A-2 and A-3 skipped). CEDAR partner_statement falls from 18000 to 0, losing 18000 (C-1, C-2 and C-3 skipped). Base code applies v1 amounts with their sign, as FEED-ATLAS-1 requires. A positive v1 RETURN (A-3 +5000, C-3 +3000) adds to sales and a negative one (A-2 -20000, C-2 -5000) reduces them. v2 is different: a RETURN amount is a size that the code turns negative, and a negative v2 amount raises an error. The PR wipes out all of the v1 handling. Only NORTHSTAR daily_sales is cleared for the 10-15 window (DH-510 and the OPS-USAGE-1004 canary). CEDAR is contractually on v1 through 2026-11-30 with no amendment. The NORTHSTAR v1 replay archives stay in scope through 2026-12-29, with no approved conversion. No rollback rehearsal or joint sign-off exists. OPS-USAGE-1001 (10-01) is an older snapshot that OPS-USAGE-1004 (10-04) replaces, and 1004 itself must be refreshed within one day of the decision. The developer note "CI is green" is guidance, not business approval.
